rules.plain_language_rule: The Hamstring Popliteal Test assesses hamstring-related knee-extension ROM with the hip maintained at approximately 90° flexion.
The non-tested leg and pelvis must remain controlled because compensation can falsely inflate the measured ROM.
Goniometric measurement is preferable to visual estimation when available.
The course reference of >70° may be used as a contextual benchmark, not as a universal diagnostic threshold.
Left and right hamstring ROM should be recorded separately.
Previous hamstring injury is a more established risk factor for future hamstring strain than flexibility alone.
Hamstring flexibility should be interpreted alongside strength, eccentric capacity, pelvic control, asymmetry, symptoms, and injury history.
Hamstring ROM restriction without pain may enter a corrective mobility pathway.
Pain during the test should stop the coach-only corrective pathway and trigger appropriate referral.
Corrective stretching should be reassessed rather than continued indefinitely without evidence of change.
